groups.title: Next.js Rendering Strategies
groups.question: You are building a Next.js site with marketing pages, a blog updated a few times a day and product pages. Explain which rendering strategy you would use for each and how you would set page metadata.

followUps.Static generation versus server-side ren: When would you choose static generation over server-side rendering?
followUps.Incremental Static Regeneration revalida: How does incremental static regeneration keep a static page up to date?
followUps.Metadata API and SEO configuration in Ne: How do you give each blog post its own title and preview tags in the App Router?

evidence.text: Static generation builds pages at deploy time, so they can be served from a CDN very fast.
Server-side rendering builds pages on each request, so data is always current.
Pages that rarely change suit static generation, while personalised or real-time pages suit SSR.
A revalidate interval marks the page as stale after a set time.
The next request still gets the cached page while a new one is built in the background.
This updates content without redeploying the whole site.

notEnough: Only saying ISR updates static pages.

evidence.text: A page or layout exports a metadata object or generateMetadata function.
generateMetadata can use the post's data to build its title and description.
Open Graph tags set how the page looks when shared.

notEnough: Only saying you set the title.

groups.title: Routing and Page Architecture
groups.question: Your blog needs a page per post at /blog/my-post and a shared layout with loading and error states. Explain how Next.js routing builds this.

followUps.File-system routing and dynamic route se: How does a file named [slug] become a page for every post?
followUps.App Router layouts, loading, and error b: What do layout, loading and error files do in the App Router?

evidence.text: Files and folders map directly to URL routes.
Square brackets mark a dynamic segment that matches any value.
The matched value is passed to the page as a parameter.

notEnough: Only saying Next.js uses file-based routing.

evidence.text: Layouts wrap pages and stay in place when navigating between them.
loading.tsx shows a fallback while the route's content streams in.
error.tsx catches errors in that route and shows a fallback instead of crashing the app.

groups.title: Next.js Optimisation Features
groups.question: Your blog's images are huge, the page jumps as images and fonts load, and Lighthouse complains about font requests. Explain how Next.js's built-in components help.

followUps.next/font for self-hosted Google Fonts w: What does next/font change about loading web fonts?

evidence.text: It serves modern formats and sizes that fit the screen.
It lazy-loads images below the fold.
Required dimensions reserve space, which prevents layout shift.
Fonts are downloaded at build time and served from your own domain.
This removes requests to a third-party font server.
Fallback font settings reduce layout shift when the font loads.

notEnough: Only saying it loads Google Fonts.

groups.title: Data Fetching Patterns
groups.question: You fetch blog posts from a CMS and want pages to be fast but still show new posts within a few minutes. Explain how data fetching and caching work in the App Router.

followUps.Server Components data fetching with asy: How does a server component fetch data without useEffect?
followUps.Caching and revalidation strategies with: How would you make cached CMS data refresh every few minutes?

evidence.text: Server components can be async and await data directly in the component.
The fetch runs on the server, so no fetching code is sent to the browser.
API keys used there stay on the server.

notEnough: Only saying server components fetch on the server.

evidence.text: Next.js can cache fetch results.
A revalidate time refreshes the cached data after that many seconds.
Data that must always be fresh can opt out of caching.
